svg.text: How a spatial query resolves
Every spatial query takes the same path: expand the region into the cells it covers, test the cluster bounds in each, then scan the clusters that overlap.
A query carrying a spatial filter — AABB, Radius, Ray or Frustum
Does the component carry a [SpatialIndex] field?
No → rejected at the call site by a debug check. It is not a runtime path at all.
yes
Was ConfigureSpatialGrid called before InitializeArchetypes?
No → the typed cluster query throws. The fluent query returns an empty set instead, which is a silent
miss rather than an error. The two entry points do not agree, and that is worth knowing.
yes
Does the query box match the archetype’s storage tier?
No → the dimensionality and precision must agree exactly. An f64 box throws as not supported;
f32 is what ships today, in both two and three dimensions.
yes
What the spatial mode decides
Spatial mode picks the half, not the path. A static
cluster is written to the cell’s static half, a dynamic
one to the dynamic half. Every query reads both
and unions them.
The static half skips fence maintenance: written at
spawn, updated on destroy, otherwise read-only.
Storage mode does not gate this. Single-version,
versioned and transient archetypes are all
cluster-backed.
A cluster belongs to exactly one cell, so a query
never meets the same cluster twice.
The per-cell cluster index — where every spatial query lands
Expand the query region into the grid cells it covers.
In each cell, test the cluster bounds. That is the broadphase.
For every cluster that overlaps, scan its occupied slots. That is the narrowphase.
All four shapes resolve here, and every archetype resolves the same way whatever its storage mode.
